Stagnation will lead to creativity. It's all part of a cycle. The human experience is one that is extremely dynamic, extremely resilient. So even though there's death, death always leads to life.

Ever since I was young, I've been able to stare in the mirror and look at who I am. I said, "This is who I am. This is what I like about myself. This is what I don't like about myself." So, I'm constantly in a process of self-reflection, self-rejuvenation, and self-invention.

I was a poor immigrant in Toronto and bullied a lot when I was young. I didn't like that. So, I worked hard and got into Yale. After I got from Yale, I thought that I would succeed in this world. But I didn't succeed. So, I looked at myself in the mirror and recognized that there were limitations to my Yale education.

I changed that. I started to reinvent myself. I did a lot of things that were experimental but which I am forever thankful for. For example, I did stand up comedy for a time. I did skydiving. I did parkour. So I am constantly in the process of self-exploration, self-reflection, and self-reinvention, which is what leads to creativity.

I wouldn't say there's a particular moment when my life changed. I would say that I've always been like that. 5 years from now, I'll probably not be the same person as I am today. I'm not content with just being who I am. I'm constantly looking to improve myself. And that means constantly engaging in a process of self-reflection. But that means also engaging a process of self-doubt and sometimes even self-hatred.

So, even though online I'm famous and people appreciate my teaching, for me what's important is whether I am improving, being creative, and contributing to the progress of humanity. These are the questions that animate me.
